meta.title: CarPal backend — risk control plan
meta.owner: Backend lead (security owner until a dedicated role exists)
meta.purpose: Register of security and privacy risks that are known but not (fully) closed by the scratch build: what can go wrong, which controls exist, what is still missing, and the plan and owner for closing each one. Started after S9b at the user's request (2026-10-24) with the staff access-purpose issue; risks found while closing S9c are added with their source.
how_to_use: Add a risk when a review, a stage report or a test finds a weakness that is not fixed in the same stage. Give it the next RCP id; never reuse or delete ids.
Rate likelihood and impact on the scales below before (inherent) and after (residual) the planned treatment; rating = likelihood x impact.
Each treatment action has an owner, a target stage and an acceptance test. Mark actions done only when the test exists and passes.
Change a risk's status only with a history entry (date, what changed, who decided). Accepted risks name who accepted them and when they are reviewed again.
dev_plan.json next_iteration items that close a risk refer to its RCP id.

likelihood.1: rare: needs several independent failures or an attacker with unusual access
likelihood.2: unlikely: needs insider access plus intent, or a secret the attacker should not have
likelihood.3: possible: any member of a common role can do it with normal access
likelihood.4: likely: reachable by ordinary users with no special knowledge
likelihood.5: almost certain: happens in normal use

impact.1: negligible: no personal or business data exposed
impact.2: minor: low-sensitivity data of one tenant
impact.3: moderate: business data of one tenant, or personal data of a few people
impact.4: major: personal data (PII) of arbitrary users, or one tenant's private records at scale
impact.5: severe: platform-wide exposure, credentials, or legal/regulatory breach across tenants

risks.title: Staff access purpose is not bound to the record being read (SEC-ADM-5)
risks.source: S9b deviations (purpose binding checked per queue item, not per record); recommendations_for_next_stages.S9 hardening list after S8; user decision 2026-10-24 to track it here.
risks.description: A staff member's CarPal-Access-Purpose header (case:<id>, dispute:<id>, dsr:<id>, verification:<id>, approval:<id>) is accepted when the named item is open in their queue or assigned to them (QueuePurposeVerifier + PurposeQueues). The verifier does not check that the record being read is the subject of that item. A moderator with any open case can therefore read the PII of any user or organization under that case's purpose; the read is audit-logged (pii.read) but with a purpose that does not justify it.
risks.scenario: Moderator M is assigned case C about a post by user A. M calls admin.user_get for user B (unrelated) with CarPal-Access-Purpose: case:C. The pipeline accepts the purpose, returns B's profile and writes a pii.read audit entry naming case C. Nothing flags the mismatch.
current_controls: admin-api reachable only through the staff gateway; staff sessions need WebAuthn aal3 with device-bound keys (SEC-ADM-1/2, GD-31).
Staff role sets per operation (STF(...)); the sweep's BFLA matrix refuses every other staff role.
PURP header required and well-formed (400 without it); the item must be open in the caller's queue or assigned to them (404 otherwise, swept for every PURP route).
Every staff PII read writes pii.read with the purpose (SEC-LOG-4; the pipeline refuses a PII response without its read-audit entry).
Mutations need a reason (RSN) and write AuditLog; DSR deletion is four-eyes (4EYES).
gaps: No link between the purpose item's subjects and the record of the request (user_id, org_id, review_id, media owner, search criteria).
admin.users_search accepts any criteria under any valid purpose.
No detective control reviews pii.read entries whose record is unrelated to the purpose.

actions.action: Purpose subjects: each PurposeQueues kind also returns the subjects of its item (case: target record, its author and organization; dispute: the parties, the review and the organization; dsr: the requesting user and their organizations; verification: the organization; approval: the review, its author and the organization).
actions.acceptance: Unit tests per kind: subjects of a fixture item are exactly the expected ids.

actions.action: Record binding: every PURP operation resolves the subject of its request (path user_id/org_id/review_id/request_id, media owner, search criteria) and the verifier admits the purpose only when that subject is among the item's subjects; otherwise 404 NOT_FOUND (no oracle). admin.users_search under a purpose is limited to the item's subjects.
actions.owner: admin module + owning modules' admin read ports
actions.acceptance: Integration test of the scenario above: user B under case C -> 404; user A under case C -> 200 with pii.read naming C.

actions.action: Contract: reword SEC-ADM-5 to 'a purpose about the record being read' and record a doc issue; regenerate the contract and the OpenAPI file.
actions.acceptance: pnpm contract:check and pnpm openapi:check green with the new wording.

actions.action: Sweep: the contract runner's admin mechanics send each PURP route with a valid purpose of an unrelated open item (another subject) and expect 404, next to the existing missing/foreign-purpose checks.
actions.acceptance: Generated suites fail when any PURP route accepts an unrelated purpose.

actions.action: Interim detective control until A2 ships: a periodic audit query lists pii.read entries whose record is not a subject of the named purpose item; the security owner reviews the list weekly once staff use the admin plane.
actions.target: before the pilot gives staff production access
actions.acceptance: Query documented in backend/README.md (admin plane) and run once against seeded data.

history.note: Found and documented in S9b (deviations_log): purpose binding is per queue item, not per record; kept for the next iteration.
User decision: track as a risk in risk_control_plan.json (RCP-01) with a treatment plan.

risks.title: Fleet drivers could read fleet records of vehicles not assigned to them
risks.owner: Backend lead; vehicle, media and ai-mcp module owners
risks.source: S9c review of the S9b BFLA scope after the user's requirement of 2026-10-24: organization-wide fleet roles see the whole fleet, drivers only the equipment linked to them.
risks.description: Role group F* contains fleet_driver, so a fleet route tagged ORG(F*) without DRV admitted a driver for every vehicle of the fleet, and records reached by id with ORG(ANY) ignored the assignment. Three leaks: vehicles.status_history on any fleet vehicle; media.get/download_url of any fleet-owned media (vehicle photos, documents); ai.suggestions_list, ai.insight_get, ai.insight_feedback and ai.suggestion_decide on the fleet's AI records (vehicle priorities, reasons, insight ids). The S9b sweep did not see them: its same-organization BFLA only tries roles outside the sec line, and a driver is inside ORG(F*).
current_controls: Contract: vehicles.status_history, appointments.history and appointments.notes_list carry DRV (the last two already filtered by the handler); SEC-AZ-7 extended to fleet records reached by id (DI-71).

Media: a driver owns fleet media only when they uploaded it or it is attached to a record of a vehicle assigned to them (AttachmentTarget.vehicleId + Authorizer.isDriverAssigned); changes are limited to their own uploads.
AI: fleet AI records are requested by FC/F+ only, so drivers get 404 on them (a driver's Help Me triage stays personal).

Sweep: a fleet-driver dimension sends the owner's request as an unassigned driver on every {flt} vehicle and appointment route the sec line opens to drivers (404, or none of the owner's records on lists); DRV routes with a path vehicle stay in the BFLA matrix.
apps/testing/fleet-visibility.int.test.ts proves each fix (all three tests fail on the S9b code).
gaps: Media attached to other fleet records (appointments, stock inquiries) only reaches a driver through their own uploads; no driver-specific rule beyond vehicles and issues exists yet.

actions.action: Fix the three leaks and add the sweep's fleet-driver dimension.
actions.acceptance: fleet-visibility.int.test.ts and the generated suites pass; the vehicle suite fails on the S9b contract (status_history without DRV).

risks.title: Fleet role model is narrower than the product expectation (operators, mechanics, dispatch, links)
risks.source: User statement of 2026-10-24: organization-wide accounts (admin, fleet manager, dispatching manager) access the whole fleet; drivers, operators and mechanics see only equipment linked to them; links are assigned by the fleet manager and the dispatch manager.
rules: 40 0.5 role groups F*, F+, FC, FR
risks.description: The contract's fleet roles are fleet_owner, fleet_manager, fleet_maintenance_coordinator, fleet_driver and fleet_viewer. Owner, manager and coordinator (FC) are organization-wide and assign drivers; fleet_viewer is also organization-wide (read-only, reports). Only fleet_driver is limited to linked vehicles, and a vehicle has at most one active assignment, to a driver. There are no operator or mechanic roles, no dispatch-manager role (the coordinator is closest), and no way to link several people, or a non-driver, to a vehicle.
current_controls: Drivers reach only their assigned vehicles everywhere (RCP-02).
Assignments are set and ended by FC (owner, manager, coordinator) with audit; ending one removes the driver's access at once.
gaps: fleet_viewer sees every vehicle; if viewers are meant to be linked staff, this over-shares.
Operators and in-house mechanics would have to be given fleet_driver (one vehicle at a time) or an organization-wide role (over-sharing).
One active assignment per vehicle: shift work or a mechanic linked to several vehicles is not representable.

actions.action: Decide the target fleet role model: map 'dispatching manager' (fleet_maintenance_coordinator or a new role), decide whether fleet_viewer stays organization-wide, and whether operators/mechanics become roles limited to linked vehicles with several links per vehicle (assignment kinds).
actions.target: before the next iteration's fleet work
actions.acceptance: Decision recorded in dev_plan.json open_questions (OQ-18) and global_decisions.

actions.action: Implement the decision: 52 role enum and FleetVehicleAssignment (kinds, many per vehicle), Docs/43 constraint and RLS, 40 role groups and DRV generalised to 'linked roles', authorizer DriverAssignments -> VehicleLinks, sweep dimension per linked role.
actions.acceptance: Sweep: every linked role reaches only linked vehicles; organization-wide roles reach all.

history.note: Opened in S9c from the user's statement; implementation waits for the role-model decision.

risks.title: Link-token validity is visible to whoever holds the token
risks.source: S9c integrity check of the BOLA expectations that are not 404 (user request of 2026-10-24).
risks.description: For a link token bound to another person (org.invitation_accept, review_invitations.verify, consents.request_view, consents.request_respond), another signed-in user gets 403 LINK_RECIPIENT_MISMATCH, while an unknown token gets 410 LINK_EXPIRED. The difference tells the holder of a token that it is valid.
current_controls: Tokens are 256-bit secrets sent only to the bound recipient; guessing is infeasible.
The 403 body carries only the Problem base (checked by the sweep): no recipient name, email or organization.
Rate limits on link operations; single-use links are consumed by the recipient.
gaps: A person who obtains someone else's link (forwarded mail) learns that it is still valid.

treatment.reason: The contract requires the distinct code so the client can tell the user to sign in with the invited account; the information is available only to someone who already holds the secret.

risks.accepted_by: Pending confirmation by the product owner (proposed in S9c)

history.note: Proposed for acceptance in S9c after the integrity check.
